boundaries.before: wire::decode of every durable message into pi_ai::Message; any lone surrogate (e.g. a tool output truncated mid-pair) rejected the whole model request
boundaries.after: For the eight APIs whose upstream request builders apply sanitizeSurrogates to user/assistant/thinking/tool-result/system text (openai-completions, mistral, openai-responses, azure, anthropic, bedrock, google, vertex; codex too except its system text), those fields and system section values are stripped of unpaired units before decoding, and each changed text is marked with pi-ai's never-serialized bits: lone_surrogates_removed on TextContent/ThinkingContent/UserMessage, and content_lone_surrogates_removed/sections_lone_surrogates_removed on SystemMessage. The SDK's emptiness checks that upstream runs before sanitizing honour them: message text/thinking/tool-result checks in anthropic, openai-completions, openai-responses, google and mistral; transform_messages; system rendering (getSystemMessageText part filter, renderSystemMessageUpdate content check, getCurrentSystemMessage collapse) and each provider's system-text presence check (anthropic system/update blocks, openai-completions, openai-responses/azure, google systemInstruction, mistral, bedrock buildSystemPrompt). Codex sends system text as unsanitized instructions, so codex system messages with unpaired units still reject. Native text never sets the bits. All other strings still reject explicitly
